players.product: grid-scale battery energy storage (BESS) for data-center/grid power

quarterly_data.signal: Fluence's fiscal 2025 key operating metrics (as of September 30, 2025): energy storage deployed 6.8 GW (+36.0%) and 17.8 GWh (+39.1%), contracted backlog 9.1 GW (+21.3%) across 33 markets in 25 countries, and energy storage pipeline 35.7 GW (+38.4%) or 122.0 GWh (+51.6%). Fluence expects to recognize approximately 55% to 60% of its remaining performance obligations as revenue in the next 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: deployed 6.8 GW / 17.8 GWh; contracted backlog 9.1 GW (+21.3%); storage pipeline 35.7 GW / 122.0 GWh; 55% to 60% of RPO within 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: Fluence's manufacturing relies on three key contract manufacturers (not named): two in the United States with facilities in Utah and Arizona and one in South East Asia; the 10-K separately notes one contract manufacturer's facility is in Vietnam. Battery module production started at the Utah contract manufacturer's facility in September 2024, incorporating battery cells manufactured in Tennessee; the Arizona contract manufacturer commissioned its facility in 2025 but encountered delays scaling production, primarily from labor availability and workforce training lead times. Fluence has supply agreements for U.S.-manufactured battery cells and U.S.-manufactured inverters (suppliers not named) and minimum purchase commitments under master supply agreements, primarily for battery cells and modules, of $205,821 thousand for fiscal 2026 and $1,195,181 thousand in total as of September 30, 2025, with $39,758 thousand of liquidated damages if minimums are not met.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 key contract manufacturers (Utah, Arizona, South East Asia); minimum purchase commitments $1,195,181 thousand total ($205,821 thousand fiscal 2026) as of September 30, 2025; liquidated damages $39,758 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Fluence's 10-K states that Siemens AG and its affiliates purchase, and are expected to continue to purchase, Fluence's products and services for energy storage projects in multiple countries, and that Fluence signs back-to-back energy storage product and service contracts with AES, Siemens and their affiliates for those affiliates' contracts with external customers.
